name: Haluski and Kielbasa (Cabbage and Egg Noodles)
writer_notes: SELECTOR: Named as a P2 hunting-ground target and nothing haluski-like is in the catalog. Buttery cabbage + egg noodles + smoked sausage is a one-skillet dish that weighs and divides cleanly at 14. Every ingredient is a tracked commodity (kielbasa, cabbage, egg-noodles, onions, butter). CONFIDENCE: source is 387 cal / 13g protein at 10 servings, which is under target; our version needs roughly a 2:1 bump of kielbasa to noodles plus cottage cheese or a leaner butter hand to land 500+ cal at 28g protein. Source numbers verified from the page, our numbers are projected. | HARVEST:
OVERRIDE Smoked Turkey Sausage: [BUMP x1.25] 10-serving haluski; 80 g sausage/serving for the 25 g floor
intro_html: Haluski is Polish home cooking in its purest form: cabbage cooked down in butter until it goes sweet and golden, tossed with wide egg noodles. Add sliced smoked sausage and it stops being a side dish and becomes dinner. Five ingredients, one skillet, 25 grams of protein, and about $2.30 a bowl (at everyday cost).
ingredients_display: Egg Noodles (Great Value wide): 36.25 oz dry (1026 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Pantry seasonings (black pepper, salt): ~$0.36. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $22.08 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.58 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $28.22 across 14 servings, roughly $2.02 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $5.36 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $33.58. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About $2.30 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a skillet dinner built on cabbage and noodles, two of the cheapest things in the store. This is what eating well on a tight week actually looks like.
shop_smart: Cabbage is the best value vegetable in the store, period. Two heads cover this whole batch and a head keeps in the fridge for weeks without wilting on you.
The smoked sausage is the budget. It is most of the cost line by itself, so buy the ropes when they go on sale and freeze them. They freeze and thaw without losing a thing.
Wide egg noodles beat fancy pasta here. Store brand twelve ounce bags are the cheapest way to buy them and the wide cut is what holds the buttery cabbage.
Do not skimp on the butter. It is one of the smallest lines on the cost list and it is the entire reason haluski tastes like anything. This is not the line to cut.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Core the cabbage and slice it into thin ribbons. Slice the onion thin as well.
Boil the egg noodles in well salted water until just barely tender, then drain them and set them aside.
Slice the smoked sausage into coins and brown them in a dry skillet until the edges char a little, then move them to a plate.
Melt the butter in that same skillet and cook the onion until it turns soft and translucent.
Add the cabbage in batches, letting each addition wilt down before you add more. Cook it slowly until it goes golden and sweet. Rushing this is the one mistake people make.
Season with salt and black pepper, then return the sausage to the pan and stir it through.
Fold the drained noodles into the cabbage and sausage in your big pot until everything is coated in butter.
portion_html: Set the full pot on your scale and subtract the empty pot weight from Step 1. Divide that total by 14 and scoop the exact amount into each container, tossing the pot between scoops so the sausage does not sink to the bottom. Every bowl lands near 595 calories and 25 grams of protein.

steps: Slice the cabbage into thin ribbons and slice the onion.
Boil the egg noodles until just tender and drain.
Brown the sliced smoked sausage in a dry skillet and set aside.
Cook the onion in butter, then add the cabbage in batches and cook slowly until golden and sweet.
Return the sausage, season, and fold in the drained noodles.
